sections.h2: One government for tax, value and deeds
sections.html:
Broomfield is a consolidated city and county between Denver and Boulder, along US 36 and US 287. Because it is both, the City and County of Broomfield runs its own Assessor, Treasurer and Clerk and Recorder under one roof at One DesCombes Drive, in the George Di Ciero City and County Building. One government assesses the value, sends the bill and records the deed.

Contacts: the Treasurer at 303-464-5810, and the Assessor at 303-464-5819 or assessor@broomfield.org.

Broomfield became a city in 1961 and a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001, assembled from land in four counties. The 2001 date matters if you are hunting for an old record: the online recording portal covers documents recorded from November 2001, and earlier ones may sit with Adams, Boulder, Jefferson or Weld.

Broomfield had 74,112 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 79,174 in July 2025, packed into 32.97 square miles. About 62.7% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $664,500. Median gross rent is $2,126. Six school districts reach into the city: Boulder Valley, 27J, Weld County RE-8, Jefferson County, St. Vrain Valley and Adams 12 Five Star. Your address decides which district's mill levy applies, so two houses a mile apart can see different bills.

Broomfield's Treasurer sets February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half and April 30 for a full payment. No interest accrues if you pay by those dates.

Tax notices go to the owner of record, not the mortgage company, around the third week of January, by email or mail. If your lender pays from escrow, check with them. Taxes under $25 must use the full-tax option.

Payment optionDue dateLate interest
First halfFebruary 281% in March, rising to 10% in December
Second halfJune 151% in late June, rising to 7% in December
Full paymentApril 301% in May, rising to 8% in December

After a due date, call 303-438-6390 for updated figures.

The Treasurer accepts cash, check, eCheck or credit card. The card provider charges 2.50%, and an eCheck costs $2.50. Online payments are capped at $1,000,000 per transaction.

A senior tax deferral program also exists, with the application at colorado.propertytaxdeferral.com. And a Certificate of Taxes Due, under C.R.S. 39-10-115, confirms that all taxes are paid except those listed as still due. Title companies often order one for a sale.

Broomfield reappraises in odd-numbered years and carries values forward in even years unless something changes. The assessment date is January 1.

The 2025 and 2026 reappraisals use residential sales from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024, and only qualified arms-length sales count. The Assessor uses the market approach for homes, and its appraisers follow USPAP guidelines.

In an even year, you get a notice only if something changed, such as a finished basement, an addition or a demolition. Tax is the assessment rate times value times tax rate. The state legislature sets the rate, while taxing authorities set the mill levy.

File with the Assessor between May 1 and June 8 for real property. Personal property protests are due by June 30.

  • Online: the appeal portal at appeals.spatialest.com/co-broomfield, which includes a neighborhood sales map and document uploads.
  • Mail: the Real Property Protest Form, postmarked by June 8, to PO Box 1149, Broomfield, CO 80038-1149.
  • In person: the Community Assistance Center in the main lobby of the City and County Building.

Useful evidence includes an appraisal dated 7/1/2022 to 6/30/2024, photos of condition, comparable sales and proof of record errors. A Notice of Determination is sent by June 30 for real property.

If you disagree, take it to the Board of Equalization, with deadlines of July 15 for real property and July 20 for personal property. Hearings are held remotely before an independent hearing officer, and you carry the burden of showing your value is more accurate. Evidence files must be 20 MB or smaller. The board's contact is clk-boe@broomfield.org or 303-438-6332, option 9. Hearings run in late July and finish by August 5.

Broomfield's fee schedule effective June 1, 2026 sets a flat $43 for the first page of a recorded document, with no charge for added pages. The recording page describes that as a $40 fee plus a $3 surcharge per document.

The documentary fee is $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500. Treasurer's, public trustee's and sheriff's deeds are exempt. The Recording Division is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and documents can be mailed, dropped off, brought in or e-recorded.

Documents need a one-inch top and bottom margin and half-inch side margins, a return address and a signed check payable to the City and County of Broomfield. The office cannot give legal advice on which document to file.

The title company pays any unpaid property tax from your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for current figures before you set a date, because interest grows monthly. A seller who closes in late winter should confirm whether the February first half has been paid.

Gather your last tax statement, your notice of value and the name of your lender if taxes are escrowed. If you pay your own taxes, make sure the owner-of-record address is current. With a cash buyer, you can skip the loan approval step, and the title company only needs the payoff and the deed to finish.

faqs.q: When are Broomfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due February 28, the second half June 15, and a full payment April 30. Interest starts at 1% the month after a missed date.

faqs.q: Does Broomfield have a separate county government?
faqs.a: Yes. Broomfield became a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001, so one government assesses, bills and records.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Broomfield valuation?
faqs.a: June 8 for real property. Appeals to the Board of Equalization follow, with a July 15 deadline for real property.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Broomfield?
faqs.a: The flat recording fee is $43 per document under the schedule effective June 1, 2026. Add the documentary fee of $0.01 per $100 over $500.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Broomfield house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing agents pay the balance from the sale proceeds. Call the Treasurer at 303-464-5810 or 303-438-6390 for the exact amount.
